queries.query: Cape Coast Ghana official cadastral map parcel GIS Lands Commission
queries.result: First-party discovery identified Ghana's Lands Commission, its Survey and Mapping Division, Central Region contact evidence in Cape Coast, Lands Commission cadastral-plan/map services, and Cape Coast Metropolitan Assembly planning collaboration. No public anonymous Cape Coast parcel viewer or ID-plus-geometry API was found.

queries.query: Cape Coast Ghana asaseɛ map parcel Lands Commission
queries.result: The local-language discovery did not expose a distinct public parcel viewer or geometry service. Ghana's official Lands Commission site advertises Twi as an available service language, but the inspected public pages remained general land-service information and did not expose parcel schema or geometry.

registry.name: Ghana Lands Commission, Survey and Mapping Division; Central Region office in Cape Coast
registry.custodian: Lands Commission of Ghana; the Survey and Mapping Division is the cadastral/survey custodian, with Central Region contact evidence in Cape Coast.
registry.scope: National cadastral and survey custodian with Central Region/Cape Coast administrative evidence; no verified open parcel layer for the city.
limitations: Official pages establish cadastral, survey, mapping, registry-map and plan services, but not an anonymous parcel data endpoint.

Cape Coast Metropolitan Assembly planning material says it collaborates with the Lands Commission Survey and Mapping Division; this is local administrative evidence, not proof of open citywide parcel coverage.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, tax, account, transaction, or personal fields were requested or retained.

sourceAssessment.reasonNoSample: No safe native parcel ID plus full polygon was returned by an anonymous public service. The official online portal exposed login-gated service pages and no public map/API configuration.

schemaCrs.details: No parcel response was obtained; native field names, stable parcel identity, geometry encoding, and CRS could not be verified.
